task_1.title: Fix APT package detection for multiarch and arch-independent installs
task_1.description: Conan 2.20.1 fixes a regression in the APT system package manager integration so installed packages are recognized with the correct architecture in multiarch environments. It also accepts architecture-independent packages during cross-building, preventing unnecessary reinstall attempts when valid packages are already present.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan's APT-based system package manager correctly recognizes already installed packages in multiarch and cross-building environments, including architecture-independent packages, so it does not misidentify valid installations or trigger unnecessary reinstalls.

expectation.grounded: The `conan.tools.system.package_manager.Apt` helper must consider an installed package as already present only when the detected package architecture matches the resolved target architecture for the request or is `all`. The same rule must apply when a version is requested, with the version also required to match before the package is skipped as already installed. This fix must cover multiarch setups where architecture-qualified package requests previously resolved to the wrong installed architecture.
expectation.conceptual: When Conan uses APT to satisfy system requirements, it should correctly detect whether the required package is already installed for the intended architecture. Cross-builds must also accept architecture-independent packages as valid, and versioned requirements must only be skipped when both the package version and acceptable architecture match.

constraints.grounded: `Apt` must not treat a package installed only for a different non-matching architecture as satisfying the request. Unversioned checks must remain architecture-aware, and versioned checks must remain both architecture-aware and version-aware. The fix is limited to package detection behavior and must not change the public package request format exposed to users.
constraints.conceptual: The update should reduce false negatives for already installed packages without relaxing package matching so far that wrong-architecture or wrong-version installations are accepted. Existing user-facing package declarations should continue to work as before.

behavior: In multiarch environments, APT-backed system package detection now identifies the installed package architecture correctly instead of misclassifying a valid installation as missing.
During cross-building, architecture-independent packages reported as `all` satisfy APT package checks and are not treated as missing solely because they are not tied to the target architecture.
When a version is specified, APT only treats the package as already installed if the installed package has both the requested version and an acceptable architecture match.
Architecture-qualified package requests no longer block correct installed-package recognition in environments where multiple architectures are available.
acceptance_criteria: When Conan checks an APT package in a multiarch environment and that package is already installed for the requested architecture, it should recognize the package as installed and skip reinstallation.
When Conan checks an APT package during cross-building and the installed package is architecture-independent (`all`), it should recognize the package as installed and skip reinstallation.
When Conan checks a versioned APT package and the installed package has the requested version with either the target architecture or `all`, it should treat the requirement as satisfied.
When only a different incompatible architecture is installed, Conan should continue to treat the APT package requirement as unsatisfied.

task_2.title: Fix Apt multiarch package detection
task_2.description: Conan 2.20.1 fixes an Apt detection regression so system requirements are recognized correctly in multiarch and cross-building environments. Packages already installed for the requested architecture, or installed as architecture-independent packages, are no longer mistaken for missing packages and unnecessarily reinstalled.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan's Apt-based system requirements handling correctly recognizes already installed packages in multiarch and cross-building environments, including architecture-independent packages, so matching packages are not reinstalled unnecessarily.

expectation.grounded: When Conan uses the `Apt` system package manager tool to check a package name, with or without a requested version, it must treat the requirement as already satisfied if the installed package for that base name is reported with either the requested architecture or the `all` architecture. This detection must work in multiarch setups and cross-building flows so Conan skips redundant Apt installs for packages that are already present.
expectation.conceptual: Conan should correctly detect existing Apt packages across multiarch environments. If the needed package is already installed for the relevant architecture, or is architecture-independent, Conan should consider the requirement fulfilled and avoid reinstalling it.

constraints.grounded: The fix must preserve version-aware and architecture-aware checks: a package should only satisfy the requirement when its installed architecture matches the requested architecture or is `all`, and when a specific version is requested the installed version must still match. Packages installed only for a different incompatible architecture must remain unsatisfied.
constraints.conceptual: Do not relax package checks so much that incompatible installations are accepted. Only already compatible packages should block a new install, and version-specific requirements must still honor the requested version.

behavior: The `Apt` tool's installed-package check should evaluate the package by its base name and determine satisfaction from the installed package metadata rather than depending on an architecture-qualified lookup alone.
In multiarch environments, an installed package should satisfy the requirement when its reported architecture matches the requested target architecture.
Architecture-independent packages reported as `all` should satisfy Apt system requirements during cross-building and should not trigger a reinstall.
When a version is requested, the package should be considered satisfied only if both the installed version matches and the installed architecture is either the requested architecture or `all`.
acceptance_criteria: When Conan checks an Apt system requirement during a cross-build and the package is already installed as an architecture-independent package, it should treat the requirement as satisfied and skip reinstalling it.

When Conan checks an Apt system requirement on a multiarch system and the package is already installed for the requested architecture, it should treat the requirement as satisfied and skip reinstalling it.
When a specific package version is requested and that version is already installed for the requested architecture or as an architecture-independent package, Conan should not attempt another install.
When only a different incompatible architecture is installed for the package, Conan should continue to treat the requirement as unsatisfied.
When the installed package version does not match a requested version, Conan should continue to treat the requirement as unsatisfied.
